A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KGAREVION and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Renamed sections and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original medical QA evaluations, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, and case-study results in Tables 2–3 and Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and adds original AfriMed-QA evaluation results in Section 4.5 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The Generate–Review–Revise–Answer procedure, TransE embeddings, attention alignment, LoRA training, and handling of unmapped entities remain unchanged. Appendix D clarifies existing Revise and Answer implementations rather than establishing new components or procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on expert multiple-choice questions from AfriMed-QA, extending coverage to African clinical healthcare and underrepresented medical contexts. The original benchmarks, MedDDx variants, and multiple-choice/open-ended tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 2–3 and the retained backbone comparisons is unchanged. AfriMed-QA reuses previously evaluated KG-Rank, Self-RAG, LLaMA3-8B, LLaMA3.1-8B, and GPT-4-Turbo. MED-ITRON disappears from the baseline prose, but it had no reported comparison results in v1.

E3.justification: The added AfriMed-QA experiment evaluates all expert multiple-choice questions using accuracy, with LLaMA3.1-8B and GPT-4-Turbo implementations of KGAREVION. Retained experiments preserve their splits, training settings, open-ended conversion procedures, and answer-order/index perturbations.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds an AfriMed-QA generalization check explicitly motivated by possible reliance on pretraining knowledge. Conversely, v1 Section 4.6 and Figure 7's worked comparison of multiple-choice and open-ended reasoning are removed. Component ablations, revision-round analyses, backbone/KG comparisons, and answer-order/index sensitivity tests remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs and standard deviations in Table 2 and specify seeds 42, 777, and 1234 in the implementation appendix. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds substantive generalization results: on AfriMed-QA, KGAREVION/LLaMA3.1 scores 55.4% versus its backbone's 50.2%, and KGAREVION/GPT-4-Turbo scores 69.6% versus 65.0%. Tables 2–3 remain numerically identical. However, v2's prose gives a conflicting LLaMA3.1 value of 55.5%, and Section 4.3 exchanges the earlier Review and Revise gain summaries despite unchanged supporting results. The worked case-study outcomes are also removed.

T1.justification: The triplet-generation definition and embedding-alignment mathematics are equivalent. v2 renames the LLM embedding dimension and replaces generic function equations with prose, without changing substantive mathematical reasoning. Neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central agent and benchmark-improvement claims are retained. v2 adds an explicit abstract/introduction claim of zero-shot generalization to underrepresented African healthcare contexts and elevates the existing input-sensitivity findings into the contribution list.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix B.3 newly interpret AfriMed-QA performance as evidence of generalization and argue that release timing and data provenance exclude leakage. The Ethics Statement adds clinical-use qualifications, including human oversight. The removed case study also removes its specific interpretation of verified triplets as an explanatory reasoning path.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository link and Appendix D's implementation walkthroughs, explicitly stating that Revise and Answer prompt unfine-tuned LLMs. Existing hardware, software versions, hyperparameters, dataset-construction instructions, and substantive prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix A surveys rule-based, graph-path, and KG-completion approaches to fact-checking, adding relevant citations. v2 also cites AfriMed-QA and removes several earlier citations, including Blois, Charles, GraphCare, and MED-ITRON. The principal positioning against LLM, RAG, and KG approaches remains.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method exposition, several results discussions, and conclusion. It retitles the paper, divides Review into explicit training/inference subsections, adds an Ethics Statement, and reorganizes the appendices. These changes substantially revise the narrative despite a stable underlying method.

P2.justification: v2 adds the AfriMed-QA bar chart, removes the worked-case diagram, and renumbers the retained sensitivity figure. Figure 2 receives label/caption edits, main table captions move above their tables, and conference headers are added. Most figures and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: AfriMed-QA supplies a useful evaluation in a distinct clinical context missing from v1, while Appendix D and the repository link improve implementation clarity and reproducibility information. These benefits are tempered by the lost worked case study and new reporting inconsistencies: Section 4.3 swaps ablation gain summaries, and the AfriMed-QA prose disagrees with Figure 6. The added evidence and documentation provide a modest overall improvement, rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper.
